quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (Anat Ashkenazi): Alphabet consolidated revenues reached $113.8 billion (17% in constant currency; full-year 2025 revenues were $403 billion, up 15%), driven by an acceleration in Search and Cloud. 'Cloud revenue accelerated meaningfully and were up 48% to $17.7 billion', driven by GCP, 'which continued to grow at a rate that was much higher than cloud's overall revenue growth rate'. GCP's performance was driven by accelerating growth in enterprise AI products 'which are generating billions in quarterly revenues', with strong growth in both enterprise AI infrastructure 'driven by deployment of TPUs and GPUs' and enterprise AI solutions (demand for models including Gemini 3); core GCP (infrastructure, cybersecurity, data analytics) also contributed and Workspace grew double digits. Cloud operating income was $5.3 billion, more than doubling year over year, and operating margin increased from 17.5% in the fourth quarter of the prior year to 30.1%. Sundar Pichai: Cloud is 'now on an annual run rate of over $70 billion'.
quarterly_data.figure: Cloud revenue $17.7 billion (up 48%); Cloud operating income $5.3 billion; operating margin 30.1% (from 17.5%); annual run rate of over $70 billion; Alphabet Q4 revenues $113.8 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Cloud backlog and deal flow (Anat Ashkenazi / Sundar Pichai): 'Google Cloud's backlog increased 55% sequentially and more than doubled year over year, reaching $240 billion at the end of the fourth quarter. The increase in backlog was driven by strong demand for our cloud products led by our enterprise AI offerings, from multiple customers.' Sundar: the backlog represents 'a wide breadth of customers driven by demand for AI products'; Google exited 2025 with 'double the new customer velocity compared to Q1'; 'The number of deals in 2025 over $1 billion surpassed the previous three years combined'; and existing customers are 'outpacing their initial commitments by over 30%'.
quarterly_data.figure: $240 billion Cloud backlog (increased 55% sequentially); existing customers outpacing initial commitments by over 30%

capex.growth: increased 55% sequentially and more than doubled year over year

quarterly_data.signal: CapEx outlook (Anat Ashkenazi): 'CapEx was $27.9 billion for the fourth quarter', in line with expectations, the vast majority in technical infrastructure with approximately 60% in servers and 40% in data centers and networking equipment; that split is 'going to be fairly similar in 2026'. 'For the full year 2026, we expect CapEx to be in the range of $175 billion to $185 billion with investments ramping over the course of the year', investing in AI compute capacity to support frontier model development by Google DeepMind, Google services, 'significant cloud customer demand' and Other Bets; 'the availability of supply, pricing of components, and timing of cash payments can cause some variability in the reported CapEx number.' Allocation: 'for 2026, just over half of our ML compute is expected to go towards the cloud business.' Depreciation rose 38% from $15.3 billion in 2024 to $21.1 billion in 2025, and its growth rate is expected to accelerate in Q1 and meaningfully increase for full-year 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 CapEx $175 billion to $185 billion; Q4 CapEx $27.9 billion; approximately 60% servers / 40% data centers and networking; just over half of 2026 ML compute to cloud; depreciation $21.1 billion in 2025 (up 38% from $15.3 billion)

quarterly_data.signal: Compute supply constraint (Sundar Pichai, asked how the 2026 capex step-up closes internal and external compute gaps): 'we've been supply constrained even as we've been ramping up our capacity'; 'some of the time time horizons are increasing in the supply chain', so how the gap closes this year 'is a function of what we have done in the prior years'. Demand across services, Google DeepMind and cloud is 'exceptionally strong', and he expects to 'go through the year in a supply constrained way'. Asked what keeps him up at night: 'the top question is definitely around capacity, all constraints be it power, land, supply chain constraints'. Anat Ashkenazi: cloud demand is expected to drive strong growth 'despite the tight supply environment we're operating in', and 'I've mentioned some of the supply chain pressures we're seeing externally'.

Accelerator mix and TPU go-to-market (Sundar Pichai / Philip Schindler): Google Cloud offers 'the industry's widest variety of compute options, from our own seventh-generation Ironwood TPU to the latest NVIDIA GPUs', backed by a ten-year track record of building its own accelerators; 'Our Cloud AI accelerators serve the leading frontier AI labs', capital markets firms like Citadel Securities, enterprises like Mercedes Benz, and governments for high-performance computing applications. Under the Reliance Jio partnership, 'Reliance Enterprise customers will also get access to Google Cloud Gemini Enterprise and TPUs'. Asked whether TPUs could move outside Google Cloud into external data centers as an incremental revenue stream, Sundar gave no separate plan and framed TPUs inside Google Cloud: 'part of what makes Google Cloud an attractive choice is the wide choice of accelerators we bring to bear here'.

Enterprise AI adoption (Sundar Pichai): in Q4 'revenue from products built on our generative AI models grew nearly 400% year over year', significantly accelerating from the prior quarter; in December nearly 350 customers each processed more than 100 billion tokens; more than 120,000 enterprises use Gemini; more than 8 million paid seats of Gemini Enterprise (launched four months earlier) have been sold to more than 2,800 companies, and Gemini Enterprise managed over 5 billion customer interactions in Q4, growing 65% year over year. Revenue from AI solutions built by partners increased nearly 300% year over year and commitments from the top 15 software partners grew more than 16x. Nearly 75% of Google Cloud customers have used its vertically optimized AI, and those AI customers use 1.8 times as many products; 14 product lines each exceed $1 billion in annual revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: GenAI-model product revenue grew nearly 400%; nearly 350 customers each more than 100 billion tokens (December); more than 8 million paid Gemini Enterprise seats at more than 2,800 companies; over 5 billion customer interactions (growing 65%); partner AI solutions revenue up nearly 300%; top 15 software partner commitments grew more than 16x; 14 product lines each exceeding $1 billion

players.product: Gemini models trained/served on TPU v7

quarterly_data.signal: Gemini model and token metrics (Sundar Pichai): Gemini 3 launched in December. 'We were able to lower Gemini serving unit costs by 78% over 2025 through model optimizations, efficiency, and utilization improvements.' Gemini 3 Pro 'has seen the fastest adoption of any model in our history' and has processed three times as many daily tokens on average as 2.5 Pro; first-party models 'now process over 10 billion tokens per minute via direct API used by our customers, up from 7 billion last quarter'; the Gemini app has over 750 million monthly active users, with a sharp increase in engagement per user in Q4; Google Anti Gravity (the agentic development platform) has more than 1.5 million weekly users. Google is 'collaborating with Apple as their preferred cloud provider and to develop the next generation of Apple Foundation models based on Gemini technology'. 2026 capex funds AI compute capacity 'to support frontier model development by Google DeepMind' (Anat Ashkenazi); Sundar expects LLM-frontier progress to continue in 2026 across pre-training, post-training and test-time compute.
quarterly_data.figure: Gemini serving unit costs lowered 78% over 2025; over 10 billion tokens per minute via direct API (up from 7 billion); Gemini app over 750 million monthly active users; Anti Gravity more than 1.5 million weekly users

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center and power build (Sundar Pichai / Anat Ashkenazi): 'In December, we announced our intent to acquire Intersect which provides data center and energy infrastructure solutions.' Sundar named the capacity constraints as 'power, land, supply chain constraints'. Anat: 'we primarily focus on construction of our own data centers. We do partner with some external parties on lease on occasion', building them to match Google's workloads. About 40% of CapEx goes to long-duration assets (data centers and networking equipment; a building could depreciate over 'forty years or longer'), and the rising technical-infrastructure investment will keep pressuring the P&L through 'higher depreciation expense and related data centers operations costs such as energy'.
